raw_text:
Here’s the complete 12-week plan summary integrating moderate-intensity cardiac safeguards, expanded strength (including safe squat/deadlift variants), higher total aerobic volume for weight loss, and the HR-capped 5K benchmark.

Safety guardrails (apply every session)
- Intensity: HR ≤ ~115 bpm (≈70% age-predicted max), RPE 3–5/10, conversational talk test.
- No Valsalva; exhale on exertion; slow 2–1–2 tempo; stop with 2–3 reps in reserve.
- Warm-up/cool-down: 8–10 min gradual ramp down/up.
- Terminate with any red flags: chest pain/pressure, unusual SOB, dizziness, palpitations.
- Progress by time/reps before load; smallest load jumps only when HR/RPE/form are stable.

Weekly structure (default)
- Mon: Resistance Upper A
- Tue: Aerobic steady (progressing to 45–60 min)
- Wed: Resistance Lower A (squat + hinge) + core
- Thu: Aerobic “upper-moderate segments” or steady (40–55 min)
- Fri: Resistance Full Body B (hinge + secondary squat) + easy cardio cool-down
- Sat: Aerobic long steady or cross-training (50–70 min by later phases)
- Sun: Recovery walk 20–40 min + mobility
- Daily NEAT: 10–15 min post-meal walks most days; steps progress toward 8–12k/day.

Strength training standards
- Sets/reps: Compounds 3–4×6–12 at RPE ≤5; accessories 2–3×10–15.
- Rest: 90–150 s on compounds; 60–90 s on accessories; extend rest to keep HR ≤115.
- Progression: Double progression (reps → load). Cluster option on trap-bar or leg press to control HR.

Aerobic training standards (weight-loss oriented within HR cap)
- Volume target: Build from ~170–200 to 260–300+ min/week by Weeks 8–12.
- Formats: Long steady; HR-capped “upper-moderate” segments; gentle incline walking; bike/elliptical cadence play.
- All sessions include 8–10 min warm-up and cool-down; stay ≤115 bpm.

Nutrition (cardiac-focused, fat-loss aligned)
- Pattern: Mediterranean/DASH; 300–400 kcal/day deficit if physician approves.
- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day; fiber 30–40 g/day; saturated fat ≤7% kcal; sodium 1,500–2,000 mg/day (or per MD).
- Hydration: ~2–2.5 L/day; moderate caffeine only if BP/HR stable.
- Pre-/post-workout: Light carb+protein 60–90 min pre; 20–30 g protein within 1–2 h post.

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation, technique, tolerance)
Goals: Establish routine, reinforce breathing, introduce squat/hinge safely, build aerobic base to ~180–220 min/week.

Week 1
- Upper A (2×12–15): Machine chest press; seated cable row; light DB incline press; neutral pulldown; DB lateral raise; Pallof press 2×10–12/side.
- Lower A (2–3×12–15): Sit-to-stand; KB RDL from blocks 3×10–12; step-ups 2×10/side; calf raises 2×15; side plank elevated 2×20–30 s/side.
- Full Body B (2×10–12): Goblet box squat; one-arm cable row; machine chest press; hip bridge 3×12 (2–3 s squeeze); face pull 2–3×12–15.
- Aerobic: 2–3 days, total 170–190 min. One steady 40–45 min; one 35–40 min with 6×2 min at HR 108–115 (2–3 min easy); one 30–40 min technique walk.
- NEAT: 10 min walk after 1–2 meals.

Week 2
- Strength: Progress most lifts to 3 sets if HR/RPE remain controlled; add single-leg press 2×12/side (swap for one step-up set).
- Aerobic: 3 days, 180–200 min; steady sessions 40–50 min; segments 6–8×2–3 min ≤115 bpm.
- Balance/mobility 1×20–25 min.

Week 3
- Strength: Keep 3 sets for primaries; accessories 2–3. Optional cluster on leg press 3×(6+6) to manage HR.
- Aerobic: 3 days, 190–210 min; long steady 50–55 min; segments 8×2–3 min; one flat-terrain pace practice 35–40 min.

Week 4
- Strength: Aim for top of rep ranges; plan tiny load bumps next week if all sets solid and HR stable.
- Aerobic: 3–4 days, 200–220 min; long steady 55–60 min; segments 8×2–3 min; 1–2 post-meal walks/day.

PHASE 2: Weeks 5–8 (Strength emphasis + aerobic volume growth)
Goals: 3 resistance days with compounds; aerobic 230–280 min/week; refine HR-capped pacing.

Week 5
- Upper A (3–4×8–12): Machine chest press; seated cable row; lat pulldown 3×8–12; DB incline press 3×8–12; DB lateral raise 2–3×12–15; Pallof 2–3×10–12/side.
- Lower A (3–4×8–12): Goblet squat (box or free) 4×8–12; trap-bar deadlift from high handles 3–4×6–10; split squat to box 3×8–10/side; calves 3×12–15; dead bug 2–3×8–10/side.
- Full Body B (3×8–12): KB RDL; landmine squat or leg press; incline push-up; chest-supported row; face pull 3×12–15; suitcase carry 3×30–40 m/side.
- Aerobic: 3–4 days, 230–250 min. Segments 8×2–3 min or 3×5 min at HR 108–115; long steady 55–60 min; one steady 40–50 min; optional 25–30 min easy.
- NEAT: 10–15 min post-meal walks most days.

Week 6
- Strength: Add 1–2 reps where possible; maintain RPE ≤5; shorten rests on accessories to 60–75 s if HR allows.
- Aerobic: 3–4 days, 240–260 min. Segments 10×2–3 min; long steady 60–65 min; one steady 45–50 min.

Week 7
- Strength: Keep loads or add small increments if top reps achieved. Add hip thrust 3×10–12; maintain trap-bar 3–4×6–10.
- Aerobic: 4 days, 250–270 min. Mixed terrain but stay flat for one “pace practice” 40–50 min at near-cap HR 110–115 after warm-up.

Week 8
- Strength: Small load increases (5–10%) on goblet squat and trap-bar if Week 7 was comfortable; optional paused goblet 2–3×5 light for control.
- Aerobic: 4 days, 260–280 min. Long steady 65–70 min; segments 3–4×5 min at HR 110–115 with 3 min easy; one 45–50 min steady; optional 25–30 min easy.

PHASE 3: Weeks 9–12 (Consolidate; HR-capped 5K benchmark)
Goals: Maintain 3–4 sets on compounds; aerobic 260–300+ min/week; practice HR-capped 5K pacing; test in Week 12.

Week 9
- Upper A: Chest press 4×8–10; seated row 4×8–10; pulldown 3×8–10; DB incline 3×8–10; cable ER 2×12–15; Pallof 2×10–12/side.
- Lower A: Landmine or heavier goblet squat 4×8–10; trap-bar deadlift 4×6–8 (cluster 3×(4+4) if helpful); step-ups 3×8–10/side; calves 3×12–15; plank elevated 2–3×20–30 s.
- Full Body B: KB RDL 3×10; goblet squat to box 3×10; hip thrust 3×8–12; row variation 3×8–12; face pull 3×12–15; farmer carry 3×50–70 m.
- Aerobic: 4 days, 260–290 min. Long steady 60–70 min; segments 10–12×2 min at HR 110–115; HR-capped progression 45–55 min; optional 25–30 min easy.

Week 10
- Strength: Add a rep or smallest load increase on primaries if two weeks stable; keep HR checks between sets.

Below is a conservative, cardiac‑rehab‑informed 12‑week general fitness program designed for a 58‑year‑old male, six months post–myocardial infarction, cleared for moderate intensity only. It adheres to: HR ≤ ~70% age‑predicted max (~115 bpm), RPE target 3–5/10, no Valsalva, no maximal lifts or strain, and gradual progression. Emphasis is on steady aerobic conditioning, light‑to‑moderate resistance training with controlled breathing, mobility, balance, and adequate recovery.

Global guidelines and guardrails
- Intensity targets: HR 100–115 bpm (or RPE 3–5/10). Stop or down‑regulate if HR crosses 115 bpm, if symptoms (chest pain/pressure, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness, palpitations) appear, or if BP response is abnormal.
- Blood pressure/medication: Confirm timing of beta‑blockers/nitrates; use RPE and talk test as primary intensity guide. Maintain nasal/diaphragmatic breathing; exhale on exertion—no breath holding.
- Warm‑up/cool‑down: 8–10 minutes each with gradual ramps, especially important in cardiac populations.
- Resistance training: Mostly machines/cables or light free weights; 2–3 sets of 10–15 reps at RPE 3–5/10, slow tempo, avoid going to failure. Rest 60–90 seconds, monitor HR.
- Frequency targets: 4–5 training days/week; split across aerobic and mixed sessions. At least 2 nonconsecutive resistance days.
- Progression: Increase one variable at a time (time before intensity; resistance via reps before load). Deload if poor recovery.
- Hydration/temperature: Avoid very hot/cold environments. Hydrate before/during/after sessions.
- Recovery: 7–8 hours sleep, daily low‑intensity walking, light mobility.
- Monitoring: Keep a simple log of HR, RPE, symptoms, BP (if available), and any medication/time. If any red‑flag symptoms occur, terminate session and seek medical care.

Program structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Re‑conditioning and technique. Build consistency, steady aerobic base, light total‑body resistance, mobility/balance.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive volume and variety. Slightly longer aerobic sessions, modest resistance progression, introduce light intervals (within HR cap).
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation. Maintain frequency, small progressions, emphasize functional strength/endurance and confidence.

Weekly schedule template (adjust days as needed)
- 2× Resistance + light cardio finishers (Mon/Thu)
- 2× Aerobic steady‑state sessions (Tue/Sat)
- 1× Mobility/balance + optional easy cardio (Wed or Sun)
- 1–2× Rest or gentle walking days

Session building blocks
- Warm‑up (8–10 min): 5 min easy cardio (HR to ~90–100), dynamic mobility (ankle rocks, hip hinges, thoracic rotations), activation (band pull‑aparts, mini‑band walks).
- Cool‑down (8–10 min): 3–5 min very light cardio; long exhale breathing; gentle stretches for calves, quads/hip flexors, hamstrings, chest.

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation and tolerance)
Goal: Establish routine, ensure safe HR response, practice breathing, build base.

Week 1
- Aerobic A (30–35 min total)
  - 10 min brisk walk or recumbent bike at RPE 3/10 (HR 90–105).
  - 10–15 min steady at RPE 3–4 (HR ≤110).
  - 5–10 min cool‑down.
- Resistance A (Total‑body; 2 sets x 12–15 reps; RPE 3–4)
  - Leg press (or bodyweight sit‑to‑stand to box).
  - Seated row (cable or machine).
  - Chest press (machine) with exhale on press.
  - Supported hip hinge: cable pull‑through or light dumbbell RDL to mid‑shin.
  - Seated DB shoulder press (light) or landmine press if available.
  - Cable Pallof press (anti‑rotation).
  - Finisher: 5–8 min easy cardio (treadmill 0–1% or bike) to HR ~95–105.
- Mobility/Balance (20–25 min)
  - Ankle mobility, hamstring flossing, thoracic rotations, cat‑camel.
  - Balance: tandem stance 3×30–45s/side, single‑leg stand near support 3×20–30s/side.
- Volume: 4 sessions this week (2 aerobic, 1 resistance, 1 mobility). Optional easy 15–20 min walk on one rest day.

Week 2
- Aerobic A: 30–40 min steady walk/bike/elliptical at RPE 3–4 (HR 95–110). Terrain flat to mild.
- Resistance A: 2–3 sets x 12–15 reps, same exercises; add Lat pulldown (neutral grip) and step‑ups to 6–8" box (assisted).
- Mobility/Balance: Progress single‑leg balance eyes open to 30–45s; add heel‑to‑toe walk 3×20 steps.
- Total: 4–5 sessions. Keep HR ≤115 at all times.

Week 3
- Aerobic B (variety): 35–40 min continuous or split (2×20 min AM/PM). Try elliptical or cycling to reduce joint load.
- Resistance B (alternate pattern; 2–3 sets x 10–14 reps)
  - Goblet box squat (light KB/DB).
  - One‑arm cable row.
  - Incline dumbbell press (light).
  - Hip bridge on bench (2–3s squeeze).
  - Cable face pull.
  - Standing cable chop (light).
  - Calf raises (bodyweight) 2×15.
- Mobility/Balance: Add dynamic marching, lateral step‑overs, and diaphragmatic breathing drills (4–5 min).
- Note: If RPE creeps >5 or HR >115, shorten intervals or reduce incline/resistance.

Week 4
- Aerobic B: 40–45 min total; include gentle terrain changes if walking. Maintain talk test.
- Resistance A or B: 3 sets x 10–12 reps, keep RPE 4–5. Progress by +1–2 reps or small load only if form and HR are stable.
- Balance circuit (10–12 min): Single‑leg stand with head turns, step‑down from 4–6" box, farmer carry light DBs 3×40–60m at easy pace.

PHASE 2: Weeks 5–8 (Progress volume and introduce light intervals)
Goal: Improve aerobic efficiency; modest strength/endurance gains; maintain safety limits.

Week 5
- Aerobic with gentle “float” segments (within HR cap)
  - 10 min easy.
  - 4×3 min at upper‑moderate (RPE ~5, HR 105–112) with 3 min easy between.
  - 5–10 min cool‑down. Total 35–40 min.
- Resistance C (3 sets x 10–12 reps; RPE 4–5)
  - Leg press or goblet box squat.
  - Seated cable row.
  - Machine chest press or push‑up to elevated bar.
  - Romanian deadlift light or cable pull‑through.
  - DB overhead press seated.
  - Pallof press + side steps with mini‑band 2×10–12 each.
- Mobility/Balance: Add hip airplanes supported, ankle/calf mobility; carry: suitcase carry light 3×30–40m.

Week 6
- Aerobic steady: 45 min continuous at RPE 3–4 (HR 95–108). Choose preferred modality.
- Aerobic light intervals: 6×2 min at RPE 4–5 with 2 min easy; total 35–40 min. Keep HR under 115.
- Resistance B repeat: 3 sets x 10–13 reps. Add single‑leg press 2×12/side if tolerated.

Week 7
- Aerobic mixed terrain walk or treadmill slight incline: 40–45 min, maintain HR ≤112–115. Practice nasal inhale, longer exhale.
- Resistance C: 3 sets x 10–12 reps; add lat pulldown 2–3 sets x 10–12.
- Mobility/Balance: Step matrix (forward/lateral/back) 3×6 each side; toe/heel walks 3×15–20m.

Week 8
- Aerobic benchmark session: 30 min at fixed pace; record HR average, RPE, and distance/speed. Compare to Week 4.
- Aerobic light intervals: 3×5 min at RPE 5 with 3 min easy; total 36–40 min.
- Resistance A: 3 sets x 12 reps; small load increases only if HR response and RPE allow. Finish with 5–8 min easy cardio.

PHASE 3: Weeks 9–12 (Consolidate and sustain)
Goal: Maintain frequency, slight progressions in time or density, emphasize functional movements and confidence.

Week 9
- Aerobic steady: 45–50 min at RPE 3–4.
- Resistance D (functional; 3 sets x 10–12)
  - Box squat or sit‑to‑stand holding light DB.
  - One‑arm cable row with slight rotation control.
  - Incline DB press.
  - Step‑ups 8–10" with rail assist as needed.
  - Hip hinge: KB deadlift from blocks.
  - Face pulls + band external rotations.
  - Carry: farmer carry light‑moderate 3×50–70m at easy pace.

Week 10
- Aerobic light intervals: 8×2 min at RPE 4–5 with 2 min easy.
- Resistance C or D alternating: 3 sets x 10–12; add calf raises 3×15 and side planks (elevated) 2×20–30s/side.
- Mobility/Balance: Clock reaches (single‑leg, supported) 2×6 each leg; gentle spinal mobility.

Week 11
- Aerobic benchmark: Repeat 30‑min fixed‑pace test; aim for equal or lower HR/RPE at same pace, or slightly longer distance at same HR.
- Resistance B: 3 sets x 12–14 reps (endurance emphasis), RPE 4–5. Shorten rests to 60s if HR allows.
- Optional second steady aerobic: 35–40 min easy cycle or swim (if competent and cleared).

Week 12
- Aerobic steady celebratory: 50–55 min conversational.
- Resistance “best form” circuit (2–3 rounds, 10–12 reps, RPE 4–5)
  - Leg press
  - Seated row
  - Chest press
  - Step‑ups
  - Cable pull‑through
  - Face pull
  - Pallof press 10–12s holds x 5/side
  - 60–90s rests; keep HR in range.
- Review week: Reassess preferences, recovery, and set next 12‑week goals.

Detailed resistance exercise notes
- Tempo: 2–1–2 (lower–pause–lift). Breathe continuously; exhale on effort.
- Range of motion: Pain‑free; avoid joint end‑range if symptomatic.
- Machines vs free weights: Favor machines/cables early for stability; introduce light free weights as tolerated.
- Terminate sets when form degrades or breathing becomes strained—do not chase failure.

Warm‑up and cool‑down example (each session)
- Warm‑up: 5 min easy bike or treadmill; dynamic leg swings, hip circles, arm circles; 1–2 light sets of first two lifts.
- Cool‑down: 3–5 min very easy cardio; seated breathing 4–6 breaths with long exhale; gentle stretches for calves, quads, hamstrings, chest.

Nutrition and lifestyle (general, unless otherwise directed by his cardiology team)
- Balanced plate: Emphasize vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, seeds, fish/lean proteins; limit high‑sodium, added sugars, and saturated fats. Consider Mediterranean‑style pattern.
- Hydration: ~2–2.5 L/day, more if warm; sip during workouts.
- Pre‑exercise: Light snack 60–90 min before (e.g., banana + yogurt, small oatmeal).
- Post‑exercise: Protein 20–30 g within 1–2 h; include fiber and healthy fats across the day.
- Alcohol and caffeine: Moderate per medical advice; avoid large caffeine doses pre‑workout if it spikes HR/BP.
- Weight management: If needed, target modest deficit (200–300 kcal/day) only with physician approval; prioritize satiety and nutrient density.

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep: 7–8 hours, consistent schedule; wind‑down routine.
- Daily movement: 5–10k steps/day as tolerated; break up sitting every 30–60 min.
- HR and RPE logging: Note average/max HR, RPE, and any symptoms; share with care team as needed.
- Warning signs to stop: Chest discomfort, unusual shortness of breath, lightheadedness, palpitations, radiation to arm/jaw, unusual fatigue—stop, sit, and follow medical plan.

Example weekly layout (Weeks 5–12 pattern)
- Mon: Resistance (C/D) + 5–8 min easy cardio finish
- Tue: Aerobic intervals (light)
- Wed: Mobility/balance + optional 20–30 min easy walk
- Thu: Resistance (alternate) + 5–8 min easy cardio
- Sat: Aerobic steady
- Other days: Rest or easy walking

This plan keeps intensity moderate, prioritizes safety, and builds aerobic capacity and muscular endurance without maximal strain. Adjust day‑to‑day based on HR, RPE, and recovery, and coordinate with his cardiac rehab recommendations and medications.

Here’s a practical, cardiologist-friendly nutrition plan aligned with secondary prevention after MI. It supports moderate training, healthy weight, lipid/BP control, glycemic stability, and inflammation reduction. Coordinate with his care team for any specific restrictions (e.g., sodium, fluid, anticoagulants, diabetes, CKD).

Core principles
- Overall pattern: Mediterranean-DASH hybrid.
- Calorie target: Aim for weight stability unless weight loss is advised by his physician. If weight loss is indicated, use a modest 200–300 kcal/day deficit.
- Macronutrient balance (approximate): 45–55% carbs (from high-fiber, low-GI sources), 20–30% fats (emphasize mono- and polyunsaturated; keep saturated fat ≤7% of total calories; avoid trans fats), 20–25% protein (lean and plant-forward).
- Fiber: 28–40 g/day from whole foods to support lipids and satiety.
- Sodium: 1,500–2,000 mg/day unless otherwise directed (check BP, meds, sweat loss).
- Added sugars: <25 g/day.
- Alcohol: Ideally avoid; if consumed, follow medical guidance and limit to ≤1 drink/day, never around training days if it affects HR/BP or sleep.
- Hydration: ~2–2.5 L/day; more if warm or exercising. Moderate caffeine only if BP/HR remain controlled.

Daily structure (simple plate method)
- Breakfast: High fiber + protein + fruit.
- Lunch: Half plate vegetables, quarter whole grains/legumes, quarter lean protein; olive oil dressing or avocado.
- Dinner: Same as lunch; include oily fish 2–3×/week.
- Snacks: Fruit, nuts/seeds (small portions), yogurt, veggie sticks with hummus, whole-grain crackers with sardines or tuna (no-salt-added).
- Cooking fats: Extra-virgin olive oil as primary fat. Avoid butter, ghee, coconut oil.
- Beverages: Water, sparkling water, unsweetened tea/coffee; avoid sugar-sweetened drinks.

Food choices and targets
- Proteins
  - Best: Fish (especially salmon, sardines, mackerel, trout) 2–3×/week; legumes (lentils, beans, chickpeas) 4–6×/week; skinless poultry; tofu/tempeh; low-fat plain yogurt/Skyr; cottage cheese (low-sodium if possible); eggs (up to 6–7/week if lipids allow).
  - Limit: Processed meats, high-sodium deli meats, bacon/sausage; red meat ≤1–2×/week, choose lean cuts and small portions (3–4 oz).
- Carbohydrates
  - Best: Oats, barley, quinoa, brown or wild rice, 100% whole-grain bread/pasta, sweet potatoes, beans/lentils, fruit (berries, apples, citrus), starchy veg.
  - Limit/avoid: Refined grains, pastries, high-sugar cereals, juices.
- Fats
  - Best: EVOO, nuts (walnuts, almonds, pistachios), seeds (chia, flax, pumpkin); avocado.
  - Limit: Cheese (use reduced-sodium, small portions), high-fat dairy, fried foods; avoid trans fats and tropical oils.
- Vegetables and fruit
  - Aim: ≥5–7 servings/day; include leafy greens, cruciferous veg, colorful peppers/tomatoes, and 1–2 fruit servings that don’t spike BG.
- Sodium-savvy
  - Choose “no salt added” canned beans/tomatoes; rinse canned foods.
  - Use herbs/spices, citrus, vinegar for flavor.
  - Read labels: target <300–400 mg sodium per serving.
- Cholesterol/lipids
  - Add 1–2 Tbsp ground flaxseed or chia daily; a small handful of nuts most days.
  - Consider plant sterol/stanol-enriched foods (2 g/day) if LDL remains high (coordinate with MD).
- Glycemic control
  - Pair carbs with protein/fat/fiber; favor low-GI options; keep even meal timing.

Sample 7-day cardioprotective menu (adjust portions to appetite, weight goals, and glucose control)
Day 1

- Snack: Apple + 10–12 almonds.

Pre- and post-workout fueling (moderate sessions)
- Pre (60–90 min): Light carb + protein, low fat/fiber to keep HR/BP stable. Examples: banana with yogurt; small oatmeal; whole-grain toast with peanut butter (thin spread).

Grocery/meal prep tips
- Stock no-salt-added beans, tomatoes, sardines/tuna, frozen mixed vegetables, pre-washed greens.

This plan pairs well with the training program: steady energy for workouts, lipid- and BP-friendly foods, and practical prep strategies to sustain behavior change.

- End-of-week: Easy 30–40 min recovery walk; debrief results and plan next cycle.

Monitoring and adjustments
- Weekly log: Session times, avg/max HR, RPE, any symptoms, sleep, body weight.
- If HR repeatedly exceeds 115 bpm at prescribed paces: reduce pace/incline/resistance, extend rest, or shorten blocks; keep total minutes.
- If recovery stalls or soreness >72 h: remove one accessory set per lift for 1–2 weeks or trim 5–10 min from one aerobic session.

Outcome expectations (if adherence is high)
- Aerobic: Increased distance covered at the same HR and lower RPE; improved HR-capped 5K time.
- Strength: Higher reps or small load bumps on goblet squat, trap-bar deadlift, rows/presses at the same RPE/HR.
- Weight: 0.3–0.7% body weight loss per week if in a 300–400 kcal/day deficit, with lean mass supported by protein and resistance training.

This 12-week plan keeps him safe within moderate-intensity clearance while delivering meaningful improvements in strength, endurance, and weight management, and provides a clear, cardiac-appropriate 5K benchmark at the end.
